task_title: close CF-245 - the disabled-pair pin is corrected fleet-wide and the lane runs; the surviving 503 class is CF-252
task_criteria: Row CF-245's three acceptance arms are each measured against the live fleet and quoted in the close record on this row. AC1, the lane no longer dies at router rating selection: after the pin correction the code-factory ops tick of 2026-11-06T00:39Z ran real board work (three closure events and worker dispatches), and the last unservable-rating tick for any code-factory lane precedes it at 2026-11-05T14:22-05:00, so zero code-factory ticks carry unservable-rating afterwards. AC2, the pin validator exists with tests in both directions: coding-hermes scheduler commit 572b111f adds internal/config/pin_registry.go plus pin_registry_test.go, where a pair marked disabled is flagged as disabled, a pair absent from the registry is flagged not-in-registry (never conflated with disabled), and an absent or empty registry yields no problems and never fails a load. AC3, the corrected pin names a pair the registry can serve: all 250 pinned fleet lanes now carry deepseek-flash/deepseek-foreman and the router registry row for that pair does not set disabled, so the row's original premise of a disabled gpt-6.1-sol/openai-codex pin no longer holds. The surviving cause of the 503 class, the router rating cliff, is tracked by CF-252 and is NOT claimed as fixed by this row. This is a verification close on evidence: no code-factory source file changes, and the row's own claim that every code-factory tick dies 503 unservable-rating is refuted at the current tip.
